properties.name: witness_type

customProperties.value: A sitting Member of Congress acting officially is a Member appearance, not a witness (ct-kw85): witness_type member_appearance, kept in the hearing's list with that label and left out of witness counts. An archive match needs the row's own state, chamber or committee role and an agreeing first name, a stated House seat whose holder's family name the row gives, a bare initial only one sitting Member in the stated chamber and state shares, or a name alone at a Member Day hearing that only one sitting Member's name fits (match_basis); several fitting Members, a former Member, a state legislator, a congressional employee and the hearing's own nominee stay witnesses, and a row that names a Member with nothing else stays a witness. A committee member's own opening statement at the hearing is a member_statement with its matched Member, not a Member appearance (owner decision 2026-11-10): the row says opening statement and the Member is seated, in the Congress of the hearing date, on the hearing's committee (the meeting's, else the print's: its own documents' committees and its own MODS committee code) or on its parent committee (a subcommittee code's first four letters and '00', since a full committee's chair and ranking member open its subcommittees' hearings but rosters seat them on the full committee only). Seated means the pinned rosters, or, for a Congress they do not hold (before the 113th), the print's own MODS committee member list.

properties.description: Witness classification: the source's (house_xml's own witness type), for GovInfo prints statement_for_record, member_statement or record_material when the entry is a statement, not a witness, and member_appearance when the archive matched a sitting Member of Congress acting officially (matched_bioguide_id, match_basis), or member_statement when that Member sits, by the pinned rosters, on the hearing's committee or its parent committee in the Congress of the hearing and the row says opening statement (a committee member's own opening statement). For member_appearance rows, and member_statement rows with a matched_bioguide_id, this is the archive's classification and replaces the source's value, which stays in the appearance record (appearance_records lake, witness_type) and the raw source body (record_sha)

properties.name: testified
properties.description: Whether the witness testified

properties.name: bioguide_id
properties.description: Bioguide identifier the publisher states for the witness (house_xml); never inferred

properties.name: superseded_by
properties.description: witness_key of the same person stated on the same meeting by a higher-ranked source (source priority, then record); null for the row to show

properties.name: matched_bioguide_id
properties.description: Member of Congress the archive matched to a member_appearance row, or to a member_statement row that is a committee member's own opening statement, holding office on the hearing date: the publisher's Bioguide ID, or the stated name and term dates (see match_basis); null on every other row

properties.name: match_basis
properties.description: How matched_bioguide_id was found. publisher_id: the source's own Bioguide ID, of a Member with a term covering the hearing date. Every other basis is archive-matched and needs a term covering the hearing date and no word of the row saying former, a closed span of years, a state legislature, a House or Senate officer or staffer, or the person's own nomination; the bases are tried in this order. The name bases need the row's last name to be a word of the Member's name_last and a first name of the row that equals the Member's first name or the nickname the members data holds (an equal first name is required when several Members fit), shares its first three letters, or spells out an abbreviated one ('Wm.'), a lone initial never counting for a full name. name_state: the row names that term's state, plus a chamber, a congressional role, or nothing but Congress and places; name_chamber: it names that term's chamber ('U.S. Senator', 'Representative in Congress', a district code like '(NM-01)', 'Rep.' alone) or 'Member of Congress', and no state; name_role: it opens a field with a chair, ranking member or leadership role of a committee, subcommittee, caucus or conference, or names a commission on which Members serve as Members (model/registries/congressional-commissions.json), names no state, and its first name agrees in full. seat: no name basis gives one Member, the row states a House seat (a state and district: '46th District; California', '(AR-2)'; a state at large: '(ND-At Large)'; or a territory's Delegate or Resident Commissioner: 'a Delegate from Guam'), names no state legislature, and a word of its name or first field is the family name of the Member holding that seat on the hearing date; no first name is needed. initial: no name basis has a candidate and no seat decides, the row names a chamber (or 'Member of Congress') and a state, one side of the first name is a bare initial ('C.' Cox in the members data, 'JD' Vance in the row) that the other starts with, and that Member is the only one sitting in the named chamber and state on the hearing date whose family name and a first-name initial the row shares. member_day: the row is a name with no other field at a hearing whose title says Member Day or Members' Day (not Former Members Day), and its family and first name agree with exactly one Member sitting on the hearing date (an equal first name decides between several). group: another source's row of the same appearance (superseded_by) matched

properties.name: person_key

customProperties.value: Archive person_key (Bioguide ID for matched Members, 16-hex hash otherwise).

properties.description: Published person identifier in people.parquet (Bioguide ID for matched/publisher Members; 16-hex person-v1 or person-singleton-v1 key for non-Members; inherited across superseded_by); null on record entries, unnamed rows, and unmatched member_appearance rows (ct-ha10)

properties.name: listing_status
properties.description: listed when present on the source's current record; no_longer_listed when an earlier Congress.gov read of this meeting listed the witness and a later Congress.gov read omitted them (ct-960v)

properties.name: last_listed_on
properties.description: Date of the latest Congress.gov read that still listed a no_longer_listed witness; null when listing_status is listed

properties.name: unlisted_since
properties.description: Date of the earliest subsequent Congress.gov read that stopped listing a no_longer_listed witness; null when listing_status is listed

properties.name: unlisted_by_record_sha
properties.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the earliest subsequent Congress.gov read that stopped listing a no_longer_listed witness; null when listing_status is listed

customProperties.value: Nullability transcribes the phase-2 annex §3 file table (docs/plans/phase-2-annex-20261028.md): a type without "nullable" there is required.

value: Sitting Members the rules cannot read stay witnesses: on the 2026-11-10 release, at least 99 shown rows, of which about 31 state an office but give a first name the members data does not hold (initial-only or middle-name Members such as T. Slade Gorton or J. French Hill, typos such as 'Partick' Leahy), 13 are print headings garbled into names, 5 state a role the rules do not read, 49 give a name alone at an ordinary hearing, and 1 a name with another Member's state at a Member Day hearing; about 20 more are question-and-answer lines of committee Members.

member_day cannot tell a sitting Member from an outside witness of the same name listed by name alone at a Member Day hearing: nothing in the row says which, and Member Day hearings sometimes also hear outside witnesses ('Member Day and Outside Witnesses', 'Public Witness Testimony'). Such a namesake would be published as that Member; none was found in this release.
The congressional commissions in model/registries/congressional-commissions.json carry statute citations marked unverified until checked against the law's text.

A committee member's opening statement stays a member_appearance when the rule cannot see it: before the 113th Congress when the print's own MODS member list omits the Member (it lists only some members); when neither the meeting nor the print names the hearing's committee; and when the print's line labels the statement only by a heading the parser does not keep in the row's fields ('OPENING STATEMENTS Crapo, Hon. Michael D.'). The print's own committee code and member list come from its MODS through the appearance records, which the lake's MODS producer does not yet fill.

value.meaning: Meeting occasion when known; package/page occasions may have no event ID.
Appearance participation in a printed hearing package; separate from ownership of submitted documents.
Bioguide identification the publisher states for a witness (house_xml); bioguide_id is never inferred. A name-matched Member is a different relationship, witness_matched_member.

The sitting Member of Congress a member_appearance row (or a committee member's own opening statement, member_statement) is, as the archive matched it: the publisher's Bioguide ID, or inferred from a term covering the hearing date and the row's own words: its last and first name (the members data's own nickname counts) with its state, chamber or committee role, a House seat it states and the holder's family name, a bare initial only one sitting Member in the stated chamber and state shares, or a name alone at a Member Day hearing (match_basis says which). Inferred matches are labelled name-matched; a name several sitting Members fit stays unmatched.

Person grouping for eligible witness appearances (Members by Bioguide; non-Members by normalized name and full normalized organization under middle-initial and suffix guards, or singleton fallback); inherited across superseded_by.
Publisher package identity; it can exist without a retained local document.
